evidence.title: Palace front of Qichun Yuan
evidence.summary: From the screen wall to the hill behind 中和堂: about 200 by 120 m. Built 1809 and called the new gate. Great and second gates are gate halls with rolled-ridge hip-and-gable roofs. 迎晖殿 is the main hall where the dowager took birthday homage. In 1986 the gates and walls were rebuilt on the site; the 迎晖殿 terrace remains.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.

plan_ref.text: Drawn on the plan of the gardens (S01), labelled 影壁.
